clue.text: Adviser was droll, without sin

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for droll surrounds the word for sin

parts.note: droll means witty
to sin is to err

explanation.surface: A counsellor used to be amusing but never transgressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. Adam Werritty was the friend and unofficial adviser whose role led to defence secretary Liam Fox resigning in 2011, topical when this puzzle ran.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Werritty was the self-styled adviser to UK defence secretary Liam Fox, a news story of 2011.

clue.text: Employed American journalist

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is crossword shorthand for a journalist

explanation.surface: A US reporter has been hired.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to use, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Murphy finds crap without crap

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: one word for crap goes round the other

parts.note: crap in the sense of excrement is poo
crap in the sense of cheap rubbish is tat

explanation.surface: Someone named Murphy discovers dung but no junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside. The two uses of 'crap' take different senses, excrement then shoddy goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy is old slang for a spud, from the Irish association with the vegetable.

clue.text: Its creed could be judicious

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A faith's doctrine might turn out to be sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ITS CREED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being judicious and being circumspect in speech or action are near synonyms.

clue.text: Said to feel absence of one jailed for failure of duty

indicators.note: said to signals that the solver should listen to how the words sound

parts.note: to feel the absence of something is to miss it, and the jail where one is held is prison: miss prison

explanation.surface: Someone reportedly pines for an inmate locked up after neglecting obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said to' makes the answer sound like MISS PRISON, what someone jailed might, perversely, feel the absence of.
explanation.definitionFit: Misprision is a legal term for neglect of an official duty, such as concealing knowledge of a crime.

clue.text: Cold after the start of a month is rotten

indicators.note: after places the cold letter behind the date piece in the answer

parts.note: the first of September can be written Sept I, using the Roman numeral for one
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A chill arriving once the month begins makes things go bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the start of a month' is read as a date, 1st September, written SEPT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something septic is infected and putrefying, so rotten in the literal sense.

clue.text: Fox's situation's sadly been lost

indicators.note: sadly here suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A fox has, alas, lost its home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges BEEN LOST. The Belstone Fox is a 1970s film (from the novel The Ballad of the Belstone Fox) named after Belstone, a village on Dartmoor in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Belstone is the Dartmoor place giving the Belstone Fox its name, so it is where that fox belongs.

clue.text: Poor Terence, caught out of course

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in a bad way, so its letters are scrambled
out means the letter for caught is removed

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Unlucky Terence was dismissed, caught, in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops C from TERENCE; 'Poor' rearranges what is left, TERENE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a course of a meal, in Britain one served before the main course.

clue.text: I stay at Maidenhead, in the same place

parts.note: to bide is to stay or wait
read as the head of Maiden, its first letter M

explanation.surface: A traveller says where they are lodging in a Thames-side town.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a Berkshire town, but here it is split as Maiden's head, M.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin for in the same place, used in footnotes as ibid.

clue.text: Short funeral hymn reflected basis for puzzles

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means the letters are read backwards
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a dirge is a funeral lament

explanation.surface: A brief lament for the dead is echoed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts DIRGE to DIRG; 'reflected' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords are built on a lattice of squares, the structure solvers fill in.

clue.text: Precede clown by one head

parts.note: an antic is an old word for a buffoon or clown
I is the Roman numeral for one
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A joker goes ahead of someone by a head.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate can mean to come before or forestall, the old sense of going ahead.

clue.text: Mostly attached by firm plaster

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: stuck means attached
CO, short for company, means a firm

explanation.surface: A coating that has nearly stuck to a solid surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims STUCK to STUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used for coating walls and mouldings.

clue.text: Mystery of exclusive order?

parts.note: something exclusive is closed to outsiders
to order a table or ticket is to book it

explanation.surface: An enigma about a reservation not open to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed book is an idiom for a person or subject one knows nothing about.

clue.text: Organ composition that requires looking into?

parts.note: the eye is an organ of the body
a piece is a musical or written composition

explanation.surface: A work for organ that needs closer study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the church instrument, but it is the bodily organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The lens one looks through on a telescope or microscope is meant to be peered into.

clue.text: Smallholder in the old sultanate?

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A small farmer in an old-fashioned Arabian state.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeoman was historically a man farming a small estate of his own, below the gentry.

clue.text: Flower is grand, as seen on the keyboard

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower
taken as written
K, for kilo or thousand, is slang for a grand

explanation.surface: A plant is magnificent, judging by what appears on the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keyboard' suggests a piano but means a computer keyboard; a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars, hence K.
explanation.definitionFit: The star-shaped symbol sits above the 8 key on a standard computer keyboard.

clue.text: Like entrance to court, or what's inside?

definitions.meaning: relating to an atrium, the entrance hall or courtyard of a Roman house
what goes on inside a court of law is a trial, so split as two words

explanation.surface: Describing the way into a courtroom, or what happens within it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as A TRIAL, which is what you find inside a court.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrial is the adjective from atrium, an entrance hall or central court.

clue.text: Some rubbish said to be found on the beach

indicators.note: said to be signals that the answer is pronounced like the words for rubbish

parts.note: rubbish dropped in streets is litter, and a coined adjective from it, litter-al, describes such rubbish

explanation.surface: Bits of rubbish are reportedly washed up on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to be' gives a word that sounds like an adjective made from LITTER, rubbish dropped in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral means relating to the shore, the zone between high and low tide.

clue.text: King of 3?

parts.note: a monarch's name that, with King in front, is also a variety of the vegetable at 3 down

explanation.surface: A ruler of a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British variety of potato, and Edward is also the name of several English kings.
explanation.definitionFit: The King Edward potato variety makes this monarch's name king of spuds, the answer to 3 down.

clue.text: Clever date arranged over the fast

indicators.note: over means the scrambled letters sit all over, that is around, the period of fasting
arranged means the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: Lent is the Christian fast before Easter

explanation.surface: A smart date was fixed after the period of abstinence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' scrambles the date to TAED, and 'over' wraps those letters around the fast; 'the fast' is the Christian season, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Talented and clever both describe someone of natural ability.

clue.text: Creature turned layer

indicators.note: turned means the letters are turned round end to end

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or plate

explanation.surface: A being that became a hen?
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' suggests a laying hen, but it is a thin layer, LAMINA.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living creature that is not a plant.

clue.text: Penalty over it must be within limits

indicators.note: over means the penalty word lies over, round, the other

parts.note: a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: A punishment for it must stay inside the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Finite means bounded, having limits or ends.

clue.text: Gaffer lost Roger — against 15?

indicators.note: lost means the letter is taken away

parts.note: a gaffer is a boss or foreman
R is the radio code letter for Roger, meaning received

explanation.surface: The boss is down one Roger, standing against a farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 across is YEOMAN; the answer rhymes with it and is a man set against one.
explanation.definitionFit: A foeman is an old word for an enemy in war, someone fighting against another.

clue.text: Mere wood at first, just in, in a word

indicators.note: at first places the wood word at the front, before the lake word

parts.note: timber is wood
a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: A pond and some trees, just arrived, in short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just in' run together reads JUSTIN, and Justin Timberlake is the American pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word, the phrase gives the first name of the singer Justin Timberlake.

clue.text: Setter's bird?

definitions.meaning: a wading bird, a kind of sandpiper

explanation.surface: Does the setter own a bird?
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius is the setter's pseudonym; the Gordian knot was the legendary knot cut by Alexander.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a stocky shorebird, and the Gordian knot belongs to this setter by name.

clue.text: Black stuff sounds like old chancellor

definitions.meaning: a black powder used as eye make-up
Helmut ... was chancellor of Germany from 1982 to 1998

explanation.surface: Dark powder sounds like a former German leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohl is the dark eye cosmetic, and also the surname of the former German chancellor Helmut.

clue.text: Well known part of a mouse in film

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Mickey, a celebrated mouse in the movies.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'of a mouse'; the surface points to Mickey Mouse, whose films made him a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous and well known are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Irrational hate follows not being quick on the draw

indicators.note: follows puts the rearranged letters after the other piece

parts.note: quick means alive, as in the quick and the dead, so not quick is dead

indicators.note: irrational means the letters are not in a sensible order

explanation.surface: Unreasonable loathing of someone slow to pull a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick on the draw' suggests a gunfighter, but 'quick' means living; 'Irrational' rearranges HATE to HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race that ends in a tie, a draw.
